newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: ATSIC COMMISSIONER WARNS OF UNREST
An Aboriginal and Torres Strait Island Commissioner has warned Prime Minister John Howard that he faces social unrest over ATSIC budget cuts and the race debate led by Independent MP Pauline Hanson.
Geoff Clark, from Victoria, says Mr Howard has allowed Ms Hanson to criticise Aborigines without check, and says as funding cuts hit, aboriginal youth will feel increasingly left out.
Mr Clark says the government that it faces increasing social unrest over its failure to address aboriginal rights - an issue he says will not go away.
He says Aboriginal people want to sit down and negotiate a future for all people, rather than fix solutions, extinguishment of Native Title and denial of rights.
CONTROVERSIAL TAXES PASSED IN NSW
A series of controversial new taxes, including a bed tax on Sydney hotels prior to the 2000 Olympics, have passed through the NSW Upper House.
The bills were passed by the Upper House at three-thirty this morning with the support of four cross-bench MP's.
NSW Premier Bob Carr says the government will proceed with a phased introduction of its poker machine tax increase from next February following the passage of its budget bills with minor amendments.
Mr Carr says the five-month delay in implementing the poker machine tax increase will cost the government 25-million dollars, but it will assist clubs and their employees.

The Transport Workers' Union says the Reserve Bank's intervention in a Transport Workers pay-claim has marked it as 'a player' in industrial relations, so the union movement now has to deal with it.
Senior TWU officials will meet with Reserve Bank governor Ian Macfarlane today to discuss bank comments which led to the failure of a the pay claim.
The bank warned there'd be inflationary pressures from a ten percent pay deal with major trucking operators before the Australian Industrial Relations Commission.
The bank's refused to speculate on the talks, but TWU President Steve Hutchins says it's a recognition by the union movement it has to deal with Reserve Bank influence.
MISSING BOY SEARCH CONTINUES
In Victoria, the father of missing toddler Jaidyn Leskie is helping police as they enter day four of their search for the boy.
Police resume their search for Jaidyn tLake Narracan and Narracan Creek.
Brett Leskie arrived in the Gippsland town of Moe last night from Kalgoorlie in Western Australia where he was looking for work.
Detectives hope Mr Leskie can help shed light on the reasons for the toddler's abduction.
Police also say bogus information about the abduction the young boy is hampering their search.
A Healsville man is alleged to be one of a number of people who have supplied misleading details - he'll be charged with making a false report and hindering police.
AMNESTY ATTACKS AUSTRALIA OVER BLACK DEATHS
Australia has come under fire for the high rate of Aboriginal deaths in custody in Amnesty International's latest report on global human rights abuses.
The report, released in London, points out that although Aborigines made up two per cent of Australia's population, they accounted for more than 20 per cent of all deaths in custody during 1996.
Amnesty International also lists claims of physical ill-treatment, harassment or intimidation of Aboriginal people by Australian law enforcement officials.
